name: View-Dependent Isosurface Extraction
text:
# View-Dependent Isosurface Extraction

Also called: View-Dependent Algorithm

## Overview
A method that extracts and renders only the visible portions of an isosurface to reduce polygon count and rendering time, exploiting depth complexity and occlusion in large datasets [S1, book]. It differs from non-view-dependent isocontouring by skipping internal sections that are occluded by the external isosurface, and from Greene's method by marking triangles as visible in software and forwarding them to graphics hardware for final visibility determination rather than rendering the visible portion in software [S1, book].

## How it works
**Inputs:** An [octree data structure](#1276-octree-data-structure.md) containing min-max values at each node, a viewpoint, and an isovalue [S1, book].
**Outputs:** A stream of triangles forwarded to the graphics accelerator [S1, book].

**Data Structures:**
1. **Virtual Screen:** A bitmap with one bit per pixel used to create an occlusion mask [S1, book].
2. **Hierarchical Tiles:** A coverage map is an 8×8 rectangular bitmap where each bit represents a pixel [S1, book]. Tiles are organized hierarchically into meta-tiles [S1, book]. Precomputed coverage patterns for edge crossings are combined to form convex polygon coverage maps [S1, book].

**Steps:**
1. **Front-to-Back Traversal:** Traverse the octree in front-to-back order relative to the viewpoint [S1, book]. Prune empty subtrees based on min-max values stored at octree nodes [S1, book].
2. **Coarse Software Visibility Test:** For each meta-cell intersecting the isosurface, perform a visibility test to determine if it is hidden by previously extracted sections [S1, book]. This step requires a front-to-back traversal to ensure previously extracted sections are already marked on the occlusion mask [S1, book].
    * **Pruning Logic:** Project the meta-cell onto the virtual screen [S1, book]. If any pixel in the projection is unset (visible), the cell is visible [S1, book]. If all pixels are set (hidden), the cell and all children are pruned [S1, book].
3. **Forward Triangulation:** Triangulate visible cells and forward the resulting triangles to the graphics accelerator for hardware rendering [S1, book]. The hardware resolves final exact partial visibility [S1, book].
    * **Rendering [Acceleration](#18-acceleration.md):** Organize tiles hierarchically [S1, book]. Project polygon onto top meta-tile [S1, book]. Recursively check only subtiles where the polygon might be visible, achieving logarithmic search [S1, book].
    * **Coverage Map Computation:** The coverage pattern of a convex polygon for a particular tile is computed by combining the coverage maps of the polygon edges [S1, book]. The coverage map of a triangle is computed from three precomputed tiles with no dependency on the number of pixels the triangle actually covers [S1, book].
    * **Difference from Greene:** Do not render the visible portion of the triangle in software [S1, book]. Mark the triangle as visible and forward it to graphics hardware [S1, book].

**Parameters:**
* **[Shear-warp](#24-shear-warp.md) factorization:** Used as a variation to reduce the cost of projecting points/triangles/meta-cells onto the screen [S1, book].
* **Tile Size:** 8×8 pixels [S1, book].

**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:**
* It is not possible to determine a priori the front-to-back relations between the triangles inside a single cell [S1, book]. Therefore, it is mandatory to accept all or none of the triangles within a cell, even though they need to be projected on the hierarchical tree [S1, book].
* A hidden cell justifies the time invested in classification because it prevents further traversal [S1, book]. A visible cell does not gain benefit from the test, adding cost to the total extraction time [S1, book].

## Subtopics

### Implicit Occlusion Test
An occlusion test for the implicit itself proposed by Pesco et al. to further reduce the cost of [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) at render-time [S2, unofficial].

## Operating characteristics
* **Complexity:** The hierarchical nature of the algorithm ensures that the cost of classification and coverage determination will not depend highly on the projected area of the cells or triangles [S1, book].
* **Performance:** Enables interactive rendering of data up to $512^3$ resolution [S2, unofficial].
* **Strengths:** Reduces the number of rendered polygons by extracting only visible portions, resulting in a faster algorithm for large datasets with internal structures [S1, book].
* **Limitations:** For larger data, interactive visualization remains difficult [S2, unofficial]. The cost of the visibility test is added to the total cost of extraction for visible cells [S1, book].

## Background
Originated from work on fast isosurface extraction methods for large image data sets, building on Wilhelms and Van Gelder's octree technique [S1, book]. It was developed to address the inefficiency of extracting internal sections of isosurfaces that cannot be seen from any direction unless the external isosurface is peeled away or cut off [S1, book].
